title: Master Shandao on Buddha-Recitation
author: Zhanran
excerpt: Question: Some monks now publicly teach that Master Shandao taught that reciting the name guarantees rebirth, and that Master Shandao taught scattered-mind Buddha-recitation. Did Master Shandao actually teach this?

inline.s: Question: Some monks now publicly teach that Master Shandao taught that reciting the name guarantees rebirth, and that Master Shandao taught scattered-mind Buddha-recitation. Did Master Shandao actually teach this?

Answer: To say that “Master Shandao taught that reciting the name guarantees rebirth” or that “Master Shandao taught scattered-mind Buddha-recitation” is to distort and slander Master Shandao. What Master Shandao actually taught was:
one must recite the Buddha’s name with a single mind, one must keep the recitation continuous from thought to thought, and one must maintain right mindfulness at the moment of death.
Where did he ever advocate that reciting the name guarantees rebirth? Where did he ever advocate scattered-mind Buddha-recitation?

blocks.text: 1. Master Shandao Taught Recitation with a Single Mind

inline.s: In
the Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra in Four Fascicles,
Master Shandao taught:
Now, practice is of two kinds: first, right practice; second, mixed practice. “Right practice” means practicing solely in accordance with the sutras on rebirth. And what is that?
With a single mind
one exclusively recites and reads this Contemplation Sutra, the Amitābha Sutra, the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, and so on;
with a single mind
one exclusively contemplates, visualizes, and recollects the splendor of the two kinds of reward in that land. If one bows, then
with a single mind
one exclusively bows to that Buddha; if one recites with the mouth, then
with a single mind
one exclusively recites that Buddha’s name; if one praises and makes offerings, then
with a single mind
one exclusively praises and makes offerings.
This is called right practice
[Single mind]
“Single” means pure and without admixture.
A single mind
means one thought following another without the intrusion of any other thought — that is, without distracting thoughts.
Bodhisattva Vasubandhu says in the Treatise on Rebirth:
“World-Honored One, I
with a single mind
take refuge in the Tathagata of Unobstructed Light pervading the ten directions
(that is, Amitābha Buddha)
, and aspire to be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss
(the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss)
Master Tanluan annotates in the Commentary on the Treatise on Rebirth:
I
, with a single mind,
” are the self-admonishing words of Bodhisattva Vasubandhu. To recollect the Tathagata of Unobstructed Light and aspire to be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss means
that one thought follows another without the intrusion of any other thought
Therefore, “a single mind” means one thought following another without the intrusion of any other thought.

blocks.text: 2. Master Shandao Taught Recitation Continuous from Thought to Thought

inline.s: In
The Pure Karma: Exclusive and Mixed Practice,
Master Shandao taught:
Continuity is rebirth
. If one can
recite continuously from thought to thought
until the end of one’s life
, then of ten, ten will be reborn; of a hundred, a hundred will be reborn.
I wish that all people would reflect well: whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, you must
exert your mind and restrain yourself
never slackening day or night
, so that when the preceding thought ends at death, the very next thought is rebirth.
Forever enjoying the bliss of the unconditioned Dharma, until at last attaining Buddhahood — how delightful that would be!
[Continuity] The thoughts of Buddha-recitation linked one after another, unbroken by deluded thoughts.
Master Shandao’s The Pure Karma: Exclusive and Mixed Practice (see
Master Shandao’s Pure Land Teachings
which explains specifically how Buddha-recitation leads to rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss
. Master Yinguang, who was a manifestation of Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta,
praised this passage most highly, saying:

“Master Shandao was an emanation of Amitābha, possessed of great supernatural powers and great wisdom. In propagating the Pure Land teaching he did not prize the mysterious and profound, but taught people to practice only in what is genuine, true, and plain.
As for the Exclusive and Mixed Practice he set forth, its benefit is boundless.
(Letters of Master Yinguang · Reply to a Certain Layman of Yongjia and His Brothers)
On the excellence of continuous Buddha-recitation,
Master Shandao taught in the Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra in Four Fascicles:
If one can recite the Buddha’s name continuously,
such a person is exceedingly rare, and nothing else can compare with them
(nothing can compare)
, therefore the puṇḍarīka is cited as a simile
(therefore the puṇḍarīka flower is used as a simile)

. As for the puṇḍarīka, it is called a fine flower among people, also a rare flower, also a flower of the highest among people, also a wondrously fine flower among people. This flower is traditionally called the cai flower. Such is one who recites the Buddha’s name:
(one who recites in this way)
— that person is a good person among people, a wondrously good person among people, a person of the highest among people, a rare person among people, the most excellent of all people.

blocks.text: 3. Master Shandao Taught Right Mindfulness at the Moment of Death

inline.s: In
The Right Mindfulness for Rebirth at the Time of Death (see
Master Shandao’s Right Mindfulness for Rebirth at the Time of Death (Annotated)
Master Shandao taught:
When one is gravely ill and nearing the end, one’s relatives must not shed tears or weep, nor utter sounds of sighing and regret, for these confuse the mind
and cause one to lose right mindfulness
The matter of death and birth is great;
one must put forth one’s own effort
If a single thought goes astray
(if the final thought at death is not right mindfulness but a deluded thought)
, one will suffer for kalpas on end — who can take one’s place? Reflect on this! Reflect on this!
What Master Shandao clearly taught is:
only with right mindfulness at the moment of death can one be reborn in the Pure Land.
How could this be “reciting the name guarantees rebirth”? Those who tout scattered-mind Buddha-recitation openly slander Master Shandao as having taught scattered-mind recitation! Let me ask:
can scattered-mind Buddha-recitation attain right mindfulness at the moment of death?
